title: MANISH KUMAR ARYA versus UNION OF INDIA

HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition Service Single No. 2040 of 2026
18th September, 2026
Manish Kumar Arya --Petitioner
Versus
Union Of India & others --Respondents
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. Vinay Kumar, learned Counsel for the petitioner.
Mr. Manoj Kumar, learned Counsel for Union of India-respondent no.1.
Mr. Anil Dabral, learned Addl. CSC with Mr. Prem Prakash Bhatt, learned Brief
Holder for the State of Uttarakhand-respondent nos.2 and 3.
Mr. Virendra Singh Rawat, learned Counsel for respondent no.4-Selecting Body.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J. (Oral)
By means of present writ petition, petitioner
has challenged the result dated 27.05.2026 insofar as it
excludes the petitioner from the final recommendation
list for the post of Instructor (Employability Skills)
under the scheduled caste category.
2. Facts, in a nutshell, are that pursuant to
advertisement dated 15.02.2024, applications were
invited for the post of Instructor (Employability Skills)
in Government Industrial Training Institutes.
Petitioner offered his candidature for the said post. He
participated in the selection process; he was declared
qualified in the written examination, and he was also
called for the purpose of document verification; but
thereafter, name of petitioner was not included in the
provisional select list.
3. It is contended by learned Counsel for
petitioner that names of four candidates were
recommended to the government for appointment by
the respondent-selecting body, but the case of
petitioner is still lying undecided, since his name did
not find place in the provisional select list.

4. This Court, vide previous order dated
08.09.2026, had directed the learned Counsel
appearing for respondent -Selecting Body to get clear
instructions as to whether the candidature of petitioner
has been rejected by the selecting body or not.
5. Today, learned Counsel appearing for
respondent-selecting body, on the basis of instructions
imparted to him, made a submission that the
candidature of petitioner has not been rejected,
however, his name was not included in the provisional
select list. Those instructions are taken on record.
6. Since the candidature of petitioner has not
been cancelled, it is not discernible as to why his name
did not find place in the provisional select list.
7. In such view of the matter, present writ
petition is disposed of finally by permitting the
petitioner to make a fresh representation to the
respondent-selecting body, ventilating his grievances in
detail, within 10 days from today; if any such a
representation is filed by petitioner within the time, so
stipulated by this Court, the Secretary of the
respondent-Selecting Body shall take decision
thereupon, within a period of two weeks from the date
of receipt of representation, strictly in accordance with
law.
8. Pending application, if any, stands disposed
of.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
18.09.2026
R.Bisht
